photo.title: A three-quarter length portrait of four men (identified as three Gumuz men and one Shilluk - probably to the right) wearing arabic-style white tunics. Evans-Pritchard notes that he met a small colony of Gumuz people, who had come from western Ethiopia in small groups over the years, around Roseires. They were (and are) predominantly muslim and besides agriculture kept small numbers of cattle and other livestock.

A three-quarter length portrait of a man (identified as the Gumuz chief) wearing an arabic-style white tunic. Evans-Pritchard notes that he met a small colony of these people, who had come from western Ethiopia in small groups over the years, around Roseires. They were (and are) predominantly muslim and besides agriculture kept small numbers of cattle and other livestock. This seems to have been the first image taken by Evans-Pritchard when preparing for his Dar Fung tour of 1926.
